title: E-Beam Inspection - Pattern Defects Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Post-Implant Quality Validation for 22nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Yuki Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify Pattern Defects defects during post-implant inspection at the 22nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 15 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Pattern Defects defects that are critical to yield at the 22nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: E-Beam Inspection
- Target Defect: Pattern Defects
- Process Step: Post-Implant
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 22nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 15

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 15 for post-implant monitoring in the 22nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v10.1.590
Recipe: E-BEAM_INSPECTION_22nm_POST_IMPLANT
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (79 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'E-Beam Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Pattern Defects defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 22nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 42 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 90% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.9% for E-Beam Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.96 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-03-17
Wafers Tested: 41
Total Defects Found: 1019
Defect Density: 324.36 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.3%
Capture Rate: 94.0%
Test Duration: 91 minutes
System Uptime: 97.6%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Pattern Defects at the 22nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
